question_text: What would happen to a buck converter if you completely removed the freewheeling Diode?
answer_text: The MOSFET would be destroyed by a massive high-voltage spike exceeding its V_DS limit.
explanation_text: According to V = L(di/dt), inductors strongly resist any instantaneous change in current. When the switch opens, the current tries to stop instantly. To maintain the current flow, the inductor transitions from acting as a load to acting as a source. Its polarity aggressively flips, making the left side of the inductor (the switch node) massively negative. Without a diode to clamp this negative spike, the switch node drops to hundreds of volts below ground. This creates a massive voltage differential across the open MOSFET, violating its maximum V_DS (Drain-to-Source) specification and instantly destroying it. You should really build this on LTspice to see it in action. An LTspice model will be added in the future if deemed necessary.
